learningObjectives.title: Arguments for the existence of God (design, First Cause)
The problem of evil and suffering

questions.q: Which thinker is most closely associated with the watchmaker version of the design argument?
questions.explain: William Paley argued that just as a watch implies a watchmaker, the ordered universe implies a divine designer.

questions.q: By what other name is the First Cause argument for God's existence known?
questions.explain: The First Cause argument is the cosmological argument, reasoning back to an uncaused first cause.

questions.q: Which Christian theologian is most associated with the First Cause argument?
questions.explain: Thomas Aquinas argued that everything is caused by something else, requiring an uncaused first cause, namely God.

questions.q: How is moral evil best defined?
options: Suffering caused by the actions of human beings
Suffering that has no cause at all
questions.explain: Moral evil is suffering brought about by human choices and actions, such as murder or theft.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of natural evil?
questions.explain: Natural evil is suffering caused by the natural world, such as earthquakes, floods and disease.

questions.q: The 'inconsistent triad' claims that the existence of evil conflicts with which two attributes of God?
questions.explain: The problem of evil argues that an all-powerful, all-loving God appears incompatible with the existence of evil.

questions.q: What is meant by a numinous experience?
options: The feeling of the presence of something greater than oneself
A dream with no religious meaning
A logical proof of God's existence
A written record of a prophet's teachings
questions.explain: The numinous is the feeling of awe and wonder in the presence of an overwhelming, holy power.

questions.q: How is a miracle usually defined in this topic?
options: An event that seems to break the laws of nature and is attributed to God
A vivid dream about the future
questions.explain: A miracle is an event which breaks the laws of nature and is believed to have been caused by God.

questions.q: What conclusion does the design argument reach from the order it observes in the universe?
options: The universe must have an intelligent designer, God
The universe came about purely by chance
The universe has always existed uncaused
questions.explain: Because design implies a designer, the argument concludes the ordered universe was designed by God.

questions.q: Why is Darwin's theory of evolution often used to challenge the design argument?
options: It explains apparent design through natural selection rather than a designer
It proves that God definitely exists
It shows the universe had a first cause
questions.explain: Evolution offers a natural explanation for the appearance of design, removing the need for a divine designer.

questions.q: Which statement best summarises the reasoning of the First Cause argument?
options: Everything that exists was caused by something, so there must be a first uncaused cause
Design in nature proves a designer
Religious experiences prove God is real
questions.explain: The First Cause argument reasons that the chain of causes must begin with an uncaused first cause, God.

questions.q: Why do many atheists use the problem of evil as an argument against God?
options: A loving, all-powerful God would be expected to prevent needless suffering
Suffering proves that the universe was designed
Evil shows that miracles are real
Suffering demonstrates that God is transcendent
questions.explain: The existence of evil suggests God is either not all-loving, not all-powerful, or does not exist.

questions.q: How does the 'free will' response defend God against the problem of evil?
options: God gave humans free will, and moral evil results from human misuse of it
God does not know that evil exists
Evil is an illusion that does not truly exist
God causes evil to punish believers
questions.explain: Free will allows genuine love and choice, but humans can misuse it, producing moral evil.

questions.q: What is the key difference between general and special revelation?
options: General revelation is available to everyone through nature and scripture, while special revelation is a direct experience given to particular individuals
General revelation only happens in dreams, while special revelation is through nature
General revelation proves God, while special revelation disproves God
There is no difference between them
questions.explain: General revelation is indirect and open to all, whereas special revelation is a direct, personal encounter such as a vision.

questions.q: What is a conversion experience?
options: An experience that leads a person to change or adopt religious faith
A logical argument for God's existence
A ceremony marking birth into a religion
questions.explain: A conversion experience so affects a person that they change their beliefs and commit to a faith.

questions.q: Why might a non-believer argue that a religious experience does not prove God exists?
options: It could be explained by hallucination, illness or the imagination
It always breaks the laws of nature
It is written down in scripture
It is shared by every single person
questions.explain: Sceptics argue such experiences may have natural, psychological explanations rather than a divine cause.

questions.q: A student says, 'The eye is so intricate and works so perfectly that it could not have happened by accident, someone must have made it.' Which argument is she using?
questions.explain: Pointing to intricate order as evidence of a designer is the design (teleological) argument.

questions.q: A tsunami destroys a coastal town, killing thousands. How would this suffering be classified?
questions.explain: Suffering caused by natural processes such as a tsunami is classed as natural evil.

questions.q: Standing alone in a vast cathedral, a visitor is suddenly overwhelmed by a sense of awe and the presence of something holy and greater than herself. This is best described as:
questions.explain: An overwhelming sense of awe and a holy presence is a numinous experience.

questions.q: A Christian comforts a grieving friend by saying that suffering can help people grow stronger and develop compassion. Which response to the problem of evil is this closest to?
options: Suffering can serve a purpose, helping people to develop and grow
Evil proves that God does not exist
Suffering is always a punishment from God
questions.explain: Some believers argue suffering has value because it can build character and spiritual growth.
